elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate
elements.evidence: no such approval shall be required for Client's assignment to an affiliate

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent
elements.evidence: Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights ... without the prior written approval of the other party

elements.element: Customer consent to Vendor assignment not to be unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: Client's approval of an assignment or transfer by TrueLink shall not be unreasonably withheld

elements.element: Vendor never to assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: TrueLink shall not assign or transfer this Agreement to a competitor of Client

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: TrueLink shall have no right to terminate this Agreement as a result of a change of control of Client

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors with written notice
elements.evidence: carve-out runs only to "Client's assignment"; no notice mechanic

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: only "Client's approval of an assignment or transfer by TrueLink shall not be unreasonably withheld" — one direction only

reasons: All six atomic preferred elements are expressly present: Customer affiliate and successor assignment free of consent, Vendor assignment gated on Customer consent, reasonableness standard on that consent, competitor prohibition, and no Vendor termination right on Customer change of control.

Edits are surgical: the existing carve-out sentence was narrowed to Client and widened to successors, plus one concise sentence for the three otherwise absent protections; no unrelated term or sentence was disturbed.
Fallback is separately not met (no mutual notice-based successor right), which is immaterial since the locked target level (preferred) is satisfied.
No undefined terms or dangling mechanics introduced; 'competitor of Client' and 'change of control' are used in their ordinary sense consistent with the rest of the agreement.
